findings.title: Budget loosening conflicts with the shopper's budget precedence
findings.problem: The tool loosens the shopper's budget by 25% and then removes it, but the system prompt ranks the budget as a hard limit where a miss is only said, and it never mentions budget loosening.
findings.proof: the budget raised by 25%, the budget removed
findings.fix: Add one sentence to the system prompt's Search rule stating whether budget loosening is allowed, and if so that the reply must name the raised or removed budget; otherwise remove the budget from the loosening order.

findings.title: Fixed-sentence priority group misclassifies no_restricted
findings.problem: Group 1 is defined as sentences that protect someone, yet it includes no_restricted, which is a shopping refusal rather than a protection.
findings.proof: 1 those that protect someone (no_harm, no_chemistry, no_restricted)
findings.fix: Move no_restricted into group 2 with the other declined items, or rename group 1 to cover all safety refusals.

findings.title: Loosening rules are duplicated between the tool and the system prompt
findings.problem: The rag.search description restates the full loosening order, which the system prompt's Search rule already summarises, so the same rule is spent twice in context.
findings.proof: Loosening: when fewer products than `top_k` meet every filter, filters are loosened in this order until enough are found
findings.fix: Keep the full loosening order in one place (the tool description) and reduce the system prompt to a pointer to it.

findings.title: Shortened spoken fixed replies duplicate the full texts
findings.problem: Eleven spoken short forms repeat the full fixed replies almost word for word, adding a second set of near-identical texts to context.
findings.proof: Spoken before a product answer, these are shortened so that the reply still fits 15 seconds:
findings.fix: Store one text per id with a short-form field only for the ids that need it, or derive the spoken form by code from the full text.

findings.title: rag.search description is longer than the decisions it supports
findings.problem: The rag.search description runs to several hundred words and repeats catalog facts that the knowledge file and system prompt already state, such as the lack of ratings.
findings.proof: Not for a current price, stock or a customer rating: the catalog has none of these (web.search does).
findings.fix: Cut the description to when to call, the filter semantics, and the output fields, and drop facts already held in the knowledge file.

findings.title: Pipeline stage descriptions repeat the enforced-by-code rules
findings.problem: The Pipeline section describes each stage's checks in detail, and the later Enforced-by-code section restates the same checks, so the critic and retriever rules appear twice.
findings.proof: Critic (rule checks in code, then a model that may report only an unsupported fact, a broken constraint without a caveat
findings.fix: Reduce each pipeline stage to a one-line role and hand-off, and keep the detailed check rules only in the enforced-by-code section.

findings.title: Fixture store labelling is not required in shopper-facing output
findings.problem: The knowledge file says 'Example' stores are recorded sample data, but the system prompt has no rule telling the reply to label fixture results, so sample stores could be presented to shoppers as real.
findings.fix: Add a rule to the system prompt that any result with provider 'fixture' is labelled as sample data in the table and spoken reply.

findings.title: No rule defines how 'best fit' ranking is made from stated constraints
findings.problem: The use case is recommendation and personalization, and the table is said to be ordered best fit first, but no rule says what the ranking is based on or forbids inferring traits the shopper did not state.
findings.fix: Add a rule to the system prompt that ranking uses only the stated constraints and cited evidence, and that no traits of the shopper are inferred.

findings.title: No rule that tool-call plans cannot be derived from tool result text
findings.problem: The Retriever may add calls in later rounds, but no rule forbids building a new tool call from text inside tool results, so an injected instruction could drive the search.
findings.fix: Add a sentence to the Retriever stage that tool calls come only from the Planner's plan and the stated constraints, never from text inside <tool_results>.

findings.title: Cache freshness is not tied to the current-price rule
findings.problem: web.search results are cached for 180 seconds and can carry cached: true, but nothing says whether a cached result may still be called a current price.
findings.fix: Add a rule that a cached web price is cited with its retrieved_at time and is not called current after the cache window.

findings.title: Spoken length limit stated in two units
findings.problem: The goal states a 15-second limit while the rule checks use a 45-word limit, and the two are not linked, so the success criterion is less clear than it could be.
findings.proof: a spoken summary of at most 15 seconds
findings.fix: State the 45-word cap once beside the 15-second goal as the test for that limit.

context_engineering.summary: The context is well grounded, with clear scope, layered safety rules and strong untrusted-data fencing, but it is heavily duplicated across the pipeline, tool description and fixed-reply sections, and it has a budget-loosening conflict and several missing controls for a personalization agent.

It has no accounts, no orders, no payments and no personal records; both tools are read-only.
